limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (e.g., base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21)

one_side_receives_without_sending.meaning: one side receives tokens without sending any

limit_order_matching_reverts.meaning: limit order matching (partial or full) reverts
limit_order_matching_reverts.checkpoint: after limit order matching is processed

assumptions: The zero-cost trade guard is the validation step whose triggering is at issue during limit order matching.
Matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities at the matching checkpoint.

unresolved.description: The intent states the guard should trigger only when one side receives without sending, but the report does not quote the guard expression or its operands, so the exact implication relation between disjoint-bit amounts and guard triggering cannot be encoded beyond grounded Booleans.
Report does not specify whether matched amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state, affecting how the disjoint-bits precondition binds.

limitations: The intent's 'only when' restriction is represented via grounded Booleans for guard triggering and the one-side-receives-without-sending condition; the precise guard expression is deferred to code binding.
The impact text describes scope (all limit order matching, partial and full) rather than a distinct numeric outcome; V is encoded as the matching revert occurrence.
